prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign LIBRA: a pair of scales seen from the front: a tall slender central pillar, a level beam across the top, and two round pans hanging from fine chains at exactly the same height. A small sun rests in one pan and a small crescent moon in the other. A single feather stands upright at the top of the pillar.

Layout, the same as the other emblems in this set: a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal, point at the top), large, almost touching the edges of the square image. The emblem sits in the middle and fills most of the hexagon, overlapping its outline slightly. Behind the hexagon, mirrored curling clouds and ribbons of wind spread outward past the frame on all sides, like the sunburst behind a sun emblem.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem or a stained-glass roundel. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical left to right, still and dignified, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no mascot, no cuteness, no story. Never fierce or scary. There is no face and no figure at all: only the scales. The sign's nature shows only through form: perfect level balance, fine thin lines, even spacing, light graceful curves: fairness, harmony, poise.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes with thick dark outlines between them, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: cream, rose pink, turquoise, lavender violet. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
